questions.explain: Collect 4–8 weeks of metrics covering a full business cycle, compute p95 and peak per dimension (averages lie), and apply a headroom policy of typically 30–50% above p95 for production.
options: Use the cloud provider's recommendation engine without validation
Average CPU over the last 7 days, then add 10%
Collect 4–8 weeks of metrics covering a full business cycle, compute the p95 and peak per dimension, and add typically 30–50% headroom above p95
Mirror the on-premises server's core count one-for-one
questions.q: What is the right-sizing measurement methodology?

questions.explain: p95 below 30% means the instance is at least one size too large. Memory pressure without CPU pressure needs a memory-optimized shape; IOPS throttling with idle CPU is a storage-tier fix, not an instance-size fix.
options: p95 CPU below 30% means the instance is at least one size too large; memory pressure without CPU pressure needs a memory-optimized shape, not a bigger general-purpose one
Average CPU above 50% always requires an immediate upsize
CXPACKET waits indicate the instance is too small
p95 CPU below 30% means the instance is correctly sized with healthy headroom
questions.q: What do the mismatch signatures tell you?

questions.explain: On RDS, modifying the instance class resizes in minutes (Multi-AZ resizes via a failover — plan timing); downsize one size at a time and observe a full business cycle, because an aggressive two-size downsize can cause a Monday-morning incident.
options: RDS cannot change instance class; a new instance must be provisioned and data reloaded
Downsize aggressively by two classes at once to maximize savings quickly
RDS resizes are always online with zero downtime
RDS modify instance class: minutes of downtime for Single-AZ, a failover for Multi-AZ; downsize in steps — one size at a time — and observe a full business cycle
questions.q: How does vertical resizing work on RDS, and what downsize cadence does the chapter recommend?

questions.explain: A database at peak 12 hours a day on a smaller tier the other 12 saves roughly a quarter of compute — more than most reservation discounts, with zero commitment — provided the scaling is automated.
options: It saves roughly half of all compute costs regardless of the schedule
A 12-hour peak / 12-hour trough schedule saves roughly a quarter of compute — more than most reservation discounts — with zero commitment
Scheduled scaling only works for storage, not compute
Manual scaling is preferred so operators can react to surprises
questions.q: What are the economics of scheduled scaling for predictable workloads?

questions.explain: Size the target from measured source metrics, not the source server's spec — the 64-core box at 15% utilization becomes an 8-vCore cloud instance — start one size above measurement for cutover safety, then downsize and revisit at 30/60/90 days.
options: Right-sizing during migration is impossible because metrics are unavailable
Size the target from the source server's spec to be safe
Size the target from measured source metrics — the 64-core on-premises box at 15% utilization becomes an 8-vCore cloud instance — then revisit at 30/60/90 days
Keep the same instance class forever once the migration succeeds
questions.q: What is the right-sizing practice during migration waves?
